text: A continuous chromia-rich scale forms the dominant completed protective barrier beneath an outer titanium-oxide-containing region.
evidence_basis: Cross-sectional SEM identifies a thick continuous chromia scale with outer TiO2 fragments.

text: Internal oxidation produces dispersed subsurface chromium- and titanium-containing oxides beneath the external scale.
evidence_basis: Cross-sectional EDS identifies internal Cr2O3, TiCr2O4, and TiO2.

text: Nickel oxide and titanium oxide are detected as secondary oxide products associated with the chromia-dominated external oxidation state.
evidence_basis: Sample-specific XRD identifies NiO and TiO2 in addition to Cr2O3.

text: The regular scale-alloy interface is interpreted as predominantly outward oxide growth associated with cationic transport.
evidence_basis: The authors associate the regular chromia-alloy boundary with mainly cationic outward growth.

text: Substantial oxide spallation removes portions of the scale and leaves locally denuded alloy surface regions.
evidence_basis: Post-oxidation characterization reports intensive scale spallation and exposed matrix regions.

text: Ti-related interaction may enhance ionic transport through chromia while the outer TiO2 layer limits chromia volatilization, producing competing effects on chromia stability.
evidence_basis: The authors propose Ti-enhanced chromia transport together with TiO2-mediated suppression of chromia volatilization.
